notes.meaning: Ezekiel gets a new message from God. He had already warned many times that Jerusalem would be ruined, and it seems he found that hard to accept. In this short chapter God helps him see why it has to happen. It also opens the way for the longer picture in chapter 16.

God asks a simple question: what makes vine wood better than any other wood? The honest answer is nothing. A vine is prized only for its grapes. God's people are often called His vine (Psalm 80; Isaiah 5; Jeremiah 2:21). They were special only because God planted them and gave them His kindness as a gift, not because of anything good in themselves. Their whole purpose was to bear good fruit for Him.

Vine wood is soft, thin, and twisted. You cannot build or make furniture with it. You cannot even carve a peg from it, the kind of wooden peg hammered into a wall in old homes for hanging pots and tools. Other trees give useful timber even without fruit, but a vine without fruit is good for nothing.

All you can do with useless vine wood is burn it. Picture a vine branch in the fire, burnt at both ends and blackened in the middle. The ends stand for the outer parts of the land, like the northern kingdom of Israel, which had already been destroyed. The middle stands for Jerusalem, which was now under attack from Babylon.
If vine wood was useless even when it was whole, it is even more useless once it is half burnt. Wood like that crumbles when you touch it. Nobody bothers to pull it out of the fire to save it.

Now God explains the picture. Just as fruitless vine wood is thrown into the fire, so He will give up the people of Jerusalem. They had failed in their task of showing the nations who the true God is. The point was to humble their pride. They had nothing they had not first received from God, and having turned from Him, they could expect only judgment.

When God "sets His face" against someone, it means He holds firm and does not turn aside until His purpose is done. The people might escape one disaster, but another would catch them. If they escaped the sword, famine or capture would follow. Each time they thought the danger was over, a new "fire" came. Through all this they would learn that God is the LORD and that His word is true.

God will make the land empty and ruined. The reason is that the people acted unfaithfully. They broke trust with Him and turned away from Him on purpose. They were not just sinners like other nations but people who abandoned the God they claimed to worship. Their unfaithfulness had gone on so long it was like one never-ending act, so the judgment was just.
